To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the supercurrent between the surfaces of a 3d topological insulator with a vortex in a narrow channel connecting the surfaces has an anomalous 4π-period term.
the superconducting current through a vortex in a topological insulator is 4π-periodically dependent on the phase difference between the two sides.
the current-phase relation of the Josephson junction with a TI slab has a 4π periodicity and that this periodicity is not related to the presence of the vortex in the junction.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the Josephson effect in a superconductor–insulator–superconductor junction, where the superconducting electrodes are covered by a thin film of a topological insulator.
a novel type of Josephson junctions based on MBS.
the study of the Josephson effect in a system consisting of a topological insulator with a vortex in a narrow channel connecting two superconducting surfaces.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Josephson effect in the presence of MBS is a very promising and promising tool for the study of the MBS.
the MBS are not necessary for the appearance of the anomalous current in the setup proposed.
the anomalous Josephson effect in the presence of MBS in the vortex core is a direct manifestation of their non-Abelian nature.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have found an anomalous term I(a)(φ)=I(a)(0)cos(4φ+φ0) in the current-phase relationship for the supercurrent between superconducting surfaces of a TI slab with a vortex in the channel connecting them.
the superconducting proximity effect in TI leads to a novel type of the Josephson effect, where the current-phase relation is 4π-periodical and has a non-monotonic dependence on temperature.
the anomalous Josephson effect is a robust phenomenon, insensitive to disorder in the TI and superconductor.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, in contrast to the usual Josephson effect, the current I(a)(φ=π) is not zero, but has the value of 2e/πh.
the MBS-induced Josephson current is not a smooth function of φ, but has a sharp maximum at φ=π.
the anomalous supercurrent is not a rare phenomenon, but rather is expected to be a generic feature of TI-based junctions with MBS.
